title: Lake plankton sample collection for molecular analysis
author: Isabelle Domaizon
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xn6fmhe
materials: The material that is classically used for phytoplankton sampling in lake is required (please see standards for the CEN if necessary). In addition, specific materials dedicated to the preparation of DNA samples are : -Gloves (at least 1 pair, 2 preferably) -Sterivex cartridge (Sterivex™ GP pressure filter units, 0.22µm; Millipore catalog# SVGPL10RC) : 1 cartridge per sample. -Caps for Sterivex (Luer-Lock male & female : outlet & inlet) : 2 per sample -Sterile Syringe with Luer lock ( Syringes BD Plastipack Luer Lock Vol 50-60mL (ref : BD plastipack H850LL) : 1 syringe per sample - Sterile bag (or tube) to store the Sterivex after filtration - Marker pen+ label OR pre-printed label for sample identification, - Field sheet + pen , - A cooling box with ice / ice packs for sample transport - Optionally a 1 L DNA free bottle that will contain a sub-sample of water dedicated to DNA (neck bottle that is larger than the diameter of the syringe) ; alternatively the water to be filtered for DNA can be taken directly from the main carboy receiving lake water samples. - Optional : scissors (to remove the Sterivex and syringe from their blister pack). Specific precautions to be taken are : - Store all materials inside DNA clean bags or containers to reduce any contamination - Wear gloves during the whole procedure - Prior to sampling, the bottles dedicated to DNA will need to be washed (H2O2 10% overnight incubation), rinsed 5X with distilled water and dry. On the field, the bottle can be rinsed with the sampled water. -In the field, before successive sampling, specific care should be taken to avoid contamination of sampling equipment: we recommend using a single bottle (that has been cleaned according to the recommendations) for each sampling station. - During the handling try to reduce exposure to sunlight if possible. - Cleaning of the water sampler, a basic option is to rinse with lake water (just before collecting the analysed water sample). - Blanks: At least one blank every 10 samples. Filter DNA free water following the same protocol as for environmental samples. The blanks will then be analyzed like other samples.

steps.title: Estimate Sampling Depth
steps.instruction: Determine the euphotic zone depth using one of two methods.

substeps.instruction: Use submersible sensors for direct measurement of euphotic depth.
Alternatively, estimate the euphotic zone by multiplying Secchi disk depth readings by 2.5 (justify if a different coefficient is used, e.g., for metalimnic cyanobacteria).

steps.title: Collect Water Samples
steps.instruction: Collect an integrated water sample representing the euphotic layer.

substeps.instruction: Use an Integrating Water Sampler (e.g., bottle IWS) or a pool of discrete samples taken with a Niskin bottle per CEN standard procedures.
Ensure the final volume is sufficient for all analyses (phytoplankton microscopic counts, DNA, and Chl-a); typically 100mL to 1L depending on lake trophic state.
Store collected water in DNA-free carboys/bottles to avoid contamination.
If transporting to a lab, use a cooling box and store at 4°C for a maximum of 12 hours before filtration.

steps.title: Prepare Filtration Setup
steps.instruction: Gather and organize all necessary materials for filtration on boat, land, or in the lab.

substeps.instruction: Prepare gloves, Sterivex cartridge and caps, syringe, scissors, absorbent paper, indelible marker or pre-printed label, and field sheet with pen.

steps.title: Filter Water Sample
steps.instruction: Filter the integrated water sample through a Sterivex unit without pre-filtration.

substeps.instruction: Remove the syringe and Sterivex from their blister pack, avoiding touching either end of the filter.
Gently homogenize the water sample.
Fill a 100mL syringe with the water sample.
Connect the syringe and Sterivex together.
Filter the water sample slowly through the Sterivex unit.
Repeat the process using the same syringe and Sterivex until the filter is clogged, noting the final total volume filtered (typically 100mL to 1L depending on microbial load and turbidity).
Ensure the total filtration process does not exceed 15 minutes.

steps.title: Preserve and Store Filter
steps.instruction: Seal and freeze the Sterivex filter for downstream DNA analysis.

substeps.instruction: Remove remaining liquid from the filter using a syringe containing air.
Cap both the inlet and outlet ends with caps or wrap with Parafilm.
Place the Sterivex in a freezable bag or a 50mL tube.
Store in ice and freeze as soon as possible at -20°C.
Label the bag or tube using pens resistant to water, humidity, and -20°C temperatures.

steps.title: Document Sampling Data
steps.instruction: Complete the sample labels and the sampling field datasheet.

substeps.instruction: Label samples with: 'Plankton', 'Lake Name', 'Station', 'Layer', 'Date', and 'volume (mL)'.
Record classical phytoplankton survey information on the field datasheet.
Record DNA-specific information: volume of water filtered, time and duration of filtration, location of filtration, and the color of the Sterivex filter.
Note the specific types of filters and syringes used if they differ from the standard material list.
